title: stream-edge-delay-corrector-and-json-tail-resilience
author: Maya Gupta
release_notes: Fix partial JSON emit when stream chunks arrive with sub-ms edge delays; improve detection of function-call/structured-output tail boundaries when heartbeats interleave. No API changes.
description:
Context: Production incidents showed a class of partial-json/structured-output failures when tiny, repeatable edge delays (sub-millisecond) caused the streamer to flush a chunk boundary that split a JSON object tail across two network frames. The OpenAI-compat adapter would then attempt to reconstruct and occasionally emit truncated JSON or mis-order function-call sentinel tokens when heartbeat/keepalive events interleaved.

Motivation: reduce user-visible malformed structured output and improve deterministic ordering guarantees for tool/function call handoff without trading off latency for steady-state traffic.

Summary:
- Add a short, bounded "edge-delay correction" window that waits for final byte drains for streams that look like they contain a JSON object tail (heuristic-based).
- Introduce a lightweight tail-coalescer that reorders late-arriving bytes within the window and keeps a small seq-anchored buffer to permit safe reassembly.
- Harden OpenAI-compat stream adapter to prefer function-call sentinel anchoring only after tail-rescue window expires or checksum verifies.
- Add deterministic ordering guard that ensures heartbeat events are treated as interleaving metadata (not JSON content) and do not close a pending structured-output span.

Checklist:
- [x] Add edge-delay window + buffer with bounded memory (50KB cap / per-stream)
- [x] Safeguard against unbounded buffering with immediate fallback to best-effort emit after timeout (25ms default)
- [x] Unit and integration tests covering split-json, heartbeat-interleave, and toolcall-ordering
- [x] CI matrix updated to include a stress test with synthetic microbursts
- [x] Docs note for behaviour change under extreme packet reordering

Commits summary:
- feat(stream): introduce edge window and tail-coalescer (main algorithm + config)
- fix(adapter): prefer seq-anchored function sentinel after tail verification
- test(stream): add fuzz/integration tests for split-json and heartbeat interleave
- ci: add stress matrix shard and timing tolerances

Changed areas (high-level):
- services/streaming/parser/edge_window_rescue.rs: implements the bounded window, voucher-based seq anchoring, and tail coalescing logic (main algorithm ~180 LOC).
- api/openai_compat/stream_adapter.go: updates to treat heartbeats as non-terminating events and to consult the rescue buffer before emitting function-call sentinels (~45 LOC).
- services/streaming/tests/test_partial_json.rs: new unit + integration scenarios exercising mid-json chunking, late-arrival bytes, and heartbeat interleaving.
- runtime/kv_cache/coalesce.py: minor change to avoid invalidating coalesced prefix when rescue buffer is active.
- docs/compatibility/streaming-edge-notes.md: operational notes and config knobs.
- ci/test-matrix.yml: stress shard added.

Small illustrative snippet (pseudo):
- before: flushOnDelimiter(chunk) -> could emit '..."content": "pa' + next frame 'rtial"}'
- now: if looksLikeJsonTail(chunk) holdFor(25ms) mergeLateBytes(seqWindow) -> emitWhenComplete or emitBestEffort

After implementation details:
- The rescue window uses a seq-anchored ledger to accept up to 3 late fragments; late fragments are only accepted if their seq id is contiguous and within the 25ms window.
- Memory bound enforced per stream; if buffer overrun occurs we fall back to immediate emit and metric to alert on overrun.
- Heartbeat frames are classified via stream metadata; classification is cheap and runs before tail heuristics.

Test plan:
- Unit tests added for heuristics and buffer edge cases.
- Integration tests with the openai-compat adapter in a real network simulator (packet reorder & microburst).
- End-to-end canary rollout to 5% of hosted API (monitor malformed-json/error-rate and function-call-order regressions).

Observability:
- Added metrics: stream.rescue.window_ms, stream.rescue.accepted_fragments, stream.rescue.fallback_emits, stream.rescue.buffer_overruns.
- Alert: stream.rescue.fallback_emits > 50/min triggers investigation.

Rollout:
- 0->5% canary with extended logging for 48h, then 5->50% if no regression, then full rollout.

Related: ENG-3284 (incident), ENG-3310 (follow-up quality gating).

Notes on tradeoffs:
- Adds a small tail latency (default 25ms) only when the heuristic detects a possible JSON tail; not applied to non-JSON streams.
- Bounded memory and timeout mitigate risk of head-of-line blocking.

Deployment: feature-gated behind feature.flag.stream_tail_rescue=false by default for immediate rollback if needed.
commits: feat(stream): add edge-delay correction window and tail coalescer
fix(adapter): consult rescue buffer before emitting function-call sentinel
test(stream): add split-json + heartbeat interleave integration tests
ci: add stress shard to test-matrix for microburst reorder
